title: Scalar restriction comparison of coherent module-transformation data
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], the ordered-fibre category $L=N(\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes})$, its pure-algebra part $A$, coherent left tensorings and module sections of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], and the operation-tree and parameterized transformation data of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction]. Let $\mathcal V$ be monoidal and $\mathcal M$ coherently left-tensored by $q:E^\otimes\to L$. Let $B,C,D$ be associative algebra sections, $h:B\to C$ an algebra transformation, $L_C$ a module section over $C$, and $N$ a module section over $D$. Put $x=L_C(m)$. Suppose $L_h$ is a module section over $B$ reconstructed from the precomposed operation and tree data of [lem-coef-module-scalar-restriction-coherence], and $e_h:L_h\to L_C$ is reconstructed from its transformation data $(h,1_x)$. Write $\Theta$ for restriction of module sections to $A$.

For every algebra map $g:D\to B$, postcomposition by $e_h$ identifies the space of coherent module-transformation data from $N$ to $L_h$ with algebra component $g$ with that from $N$ to $L_C$ with algebra component $hg$. The comparison preserves the underlying map $f:N(m)\to x$ and identifies the operation-naturality data by
$$f\,b^N_r\simeq b^{L_C}_r((hg)^{\otimes r}\otimes f)=b^{L_h}_r(g^{\otimes r}\otimes f).$$
The last equality uses the specified coherent composition of the tensor action. This identification includes all operation-tree comparisons and all chains of contractions, rather than only these displayed equations. It has a coherent inverse, is natural in $N$ and in $g$, and holds over every simplicial family of algebra maps $g$, compatibly with restriction of parameters. Thus it identifies the full spaces of such transformation data over $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(D,B)$, not merely their sets of components. The forward comparison reconstructs to postcomposition with $e_h$. The assertion concerns operation data and does not assume that $\Theta$ is a cartesian fibration. No presentability or colimit hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Put $y=N(m)$. Apply [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] to the two-color operad described in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Thus transformations, with their higher parameter simplices, are maps on color objects together with operation-naturality simplices and their tree-contraction compatibilities. Fix the pure-algebra transformation $g$ on the left and the specified coherent composite $hg$ on the right. Denote these transformation spaces by $T_h(g)$ and $T_C(hg)$. The comparison in the assertion is over the space of $g$'s: its target is pulled back along $g\mapsto hg$, retaining $g$ as part of the data. In particular it does not ask to recover $g$ from $hg$. A point on either side has a module-color map $f:y\to x$. Throughout, fixed-component spaces mean homotopy fibers; the coherent paths specifying the components are retained. This agrees with the parameterized operation-data description and avoids replacing spaces by sets of homotopy classes.

proof.text:
For every ordered operation with $r$ algebra inputs and one module input, put
$$a_r=f\,b^N_r,\quad c_r=b^{L_h}_r(g^{\otimes r}\otimes f),\quad d_r=b^{L_C}_r((hg)^{\otimes r}\otimes f).$$
The given scalar-restriction data of [lem-coef-module-scalar-restriction-coherence] identifies $b^{L_h}_r$ with $b^{L_C}_r(h^{\otimes r}\otimes1_x)$. Substitute this expression into $c_r$. Functoriality of the specified iterated tensor action composes the $g$'s with the $h$'s and composes $f$ with $1_x$, giving a specified path $\sigma_r:c_r\simeq d_r$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(D^{\otimes r}\otimes y,x)$. Thus the two naturality conditions are paths from $a_r$ to the two coherently identified endpoints. At $r=0$ the comparison uses the unit compatibility of $h$ and the identity constraint on $x$; it imposes no extra equation on $f$. Pure-algebra operations have the already specified composite transformation $hg$.

proof.text: Check the endpoint identification for the whole indexing system, not just one operation. A tree with module output has a unique module-input branch: at each vertex on it the other incoming subtrees have only algebra colors. Label those subtrees by the specified algebra transformation $h$, and label the module branch by the substitution data of $L_C$ and its module-color identity. This is exactly the tree construction supplied in [lem-coef-module-scalar-restriction-coherence]. Precompose the external algebra inputs by $g$ and the module input by $f$. A contraction within an algebra subtree uses the corresponding coherence of $g$, $h$, and their specified composite; a contraction meeting the module branch uses the substitution coherence just cited. Consequently the two restrictions on each contraction face are the same prescribed comparison. For a chain of contractions the higher comparison supplied by that node gives the prism between these faces. Grafting, permutations and insertion of identities use the corresponding clauses of that node. Forests are the products of their output-tree data by [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction]; discarded inputs are omitted, while the subinterval trees before an input is discarded are retained. We have therefore identified the entire coherent endpoint system for the module-naturality data.

proof.text:
Here is the boundary-lifting argument used to implement that identification on all the data. The mapping spaces carrying the operation and contraction comparisons are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. If $Z$ is any one of these spaces, $P\subseteq Q$ a specified union of faces, and a boundary homotopy is prescribed on $P\times\Delta^1$, an existing comparison on $Q\times\{0\}$ extends across $Q\times\Delta^1$. Indeed the inclusion
$$(P\times\Delta^1)\cup(Q\times\{0\})\hookrightarrow Q\times\Delta^1$$
is the pushout-product of the monomorphism $P\hookrightarrow Q$ and the endpoint horn $\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. It is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], so it lifts against $Z\to *$. The same assertion with an additional parameter boundary follows by using that parameter boundary in the monomorphism. It follows that the space of these extensions is contractible whenever the prescribed data exist: lifting any boundary of parameters is the same pushout-product calculation, including the empty boundary for existence. Equivalently its map to a point is a trivial Kan fibration, by [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]. This argument is relative to any faces already fixed; it does not require their comparison spaces to be contractible.

proof.text: For a point of $T_h(g)$ concatenate each operation-naturality path $a_r\simeq c_r$ with $\sigma_r$ to obtain $a_r\simeq d_r$. For its higher tree data do the same pasting along the coherent endpoint prisms of step 3. Construct it in increasing simplex dimension, fixing all faces already constructed; step 4 supplies each relative prism. Include all tree indices at a given dimension and their parameter simplices in this construction. Faces for contractions, graftings and identities are the prescribed ones of step 3, so the lifts agree on their intersections. Degenerate simplices are assigned their already specified degeneracies. This defines the forward comparison of coherent data, with module component still $f$ and algebra component $hg$. Reversing each endpoint prism and concatenating with $\sigma_r^{-1}$ gives the reverse construction with pure-algebra component the retained $g$. Inverting these paths is possible because their ambient mapping spaces are Kan: every edge there is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. No inverse of the algebra map $h$ is used. The arbitrary parameter-boundary clause in step 4 makes the compatible choices contractible, rather than choosing unrelated fillers for individual families.

proof.text: The two composites paste an endpoint prism and its reverse. In each Kan comparison space the inverse-triangle homotopies contract these pastings to the constant prism; the algebra component remains the specified $g$ (respectively $hg$) and the module component remains $f$. Supply the contractions on all tree indices together, relative to their already fixed faces, using the parameter-boundary calculation of step 4. Its contractible extension spaces also fill the higher compatibilities between these contractions. This gives coherent inverse homotopies on the full transformation-data spaces. In particular the calculation proves an equivalence even when these spaces are empty; it never assumed the existence of a module map with prescribed $f$. Concatenation and the inverse triangles here are compositions and inverse witnesses in Kan mapping spaces, justified by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] and [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration].

proof.text: Identify the forward map. A composite $N\to L_h\xrightarrow{e_h}L_C$ has color maps $(hg,1_xf)=(hg,f)$. Its naturality prism for an operation is the naturality prism of the first transformation pasted with that of $e_h$, evaluated on $(g,f)$. The latter is exactly $\sigma_r$ by the definition of $e_h$ in the hypothesis and [lem-coef-module-scalar-restriction-coherence]. The same pasting for a chain of tree contractions is exactly the prism used in steps 3 and 5. Thus the forward map is the operation-data expression of postcomposition with $e_h$. Reconstruction identifies these pastings with coherent transformations and their composition by [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], including its contractible identified reconstruction spaces. This verifies the specified forward map rather than merely producing an abstract equivalence between two spaces.

source.place: Definitions 4.2.1.7, 4.2.1.13 and 4.2.1.19; agent operation-data proof of the scalar-restriction comparison underlying Corollary 4.2.3.2, printed p. 527. The corollary is a check on the result, not a premise.

proof.text: Finally make the construction with a simplicial parameter $K$. The given scalar-restriction coherence and the reconstruction equivalence both hold over every $K$ and commute with restriction. All the expressions above are obtained by evaluating these fixed data, tensoring, composition and common diagonal restriction in the parameters; hence pulling back along $K'\to K$ gives the same boundary prisms and the same comparison. Relative parameter boundaries were included in step 4, so the inverse comparisons and inverse homotopies exist coherently over the entire space of $g$'s. Precomposing a transformation out of $N$ pastes its operation prisms before those above. Associativity of this pasting, including its higher simplices, gives naturality in $N$; it is also natural in coherent changes of $g$. Alternatively the forward map is the postcomposition map identified in step 7, so all these naturality diagrams are its composition simplices. Pointwise equivalences are equivalences in the coherent functor category by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], providing a coherent natural inverse. The displayed formula, the equivalence over $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(D,B)$ and all parameter compatibilities now follow. All lifting occurred in mapping spaces of the specified action; no cartesian-fibration property of $\Theta$ and no presentability or colimit hypothesis entered.
